title: Lab 2 - 2026

lab_objective.description: By the end of this lab, you will be able to create directory structures, manage files, copy files between locations, redirect command output, and inspect file contents using common Linux filesystem commands.
lab_objective.scenario: You have been assigned to organize system files for a Linux server. As a Junior Linux Administrator, your task is to create the required directory structure, manage configuration files, copy important system files, redirect command output into files, and verify file contents using standard Linux commands.
prerequisites: User account with write permission to the home directory
objectives: Create text files using output redirection.
View the beginning and end of files using head and tail.
Identify file types using the file command.
Understand when rmdir succeeds and fails.

tasks.title: Prepare the Working Environment
steps: Login to the Linux server.
Open the Terminal.
Navigate to your home directory.
Perform all tasks from your home directory unless otherwise instructed.

tasks.title: Create Directory Structure
steps: Create the following nested directory structure:
vars/systems/logs

tasks.title: Create an Empty File
steps: Navigate to the vars/systems directory.
Create an empty file named 'dmesg'.

tasks.title: Create a Text File
steps: Navigate to vars/systems/logs.
Create a file named 'file1.txt'.
Store the following text inside the file:
I love Linux and am excited to join the DevOps course.

tasks.title: Create Another Directory Structure
steps: Create the following directory structure:
vars/os/configs

tasks.title: Copy System Configuration File
steps: Copy the '/etc/hosts' file into the vars/os/configs directory.

tasks.title: Copy Hosts File
steps: Copy the hosts file from vars/os/configs into the vars directory.

tasks.title: Display File Contents
steps: Use the cat command to display the contents of the hosts file located inside the vars directory.

tasks.title: Redirect Output into a New File
steps: Display the contents of the hosts file using the cat command.
Redirect the output into a new file named 'new_hosts'.
Store the new file inside vars/os/configs.

tasks.title: Copy and Rename a File
steps: Copy file1.txt from vars/systems/logs into the vars/os directory.
Rename the copied file as 'new_file1.txt' during the copy operation.

tasks.title: Create Additional Files
steps: Inside vars/systems/logs create the following empty files:
sshd_config
httpd.conf

tasks.title: Create Another Text File
steps: Inside vars/systems create a file named 'new_file.txt'.
Store the following text inside the file:
I am enjoying DevOps sessions and lab work.

tasks.title: Remove a Directory
steps: Attempt to remove the vars/os/configs directory using the rmdir command.
Observe whether the command succeeds or fails.
Understand why rmdir cannot remove a directory that contains files.

tasks.title: Display Last Lines of a File
steps: Display the last five lines of /etc/nsswitch.conf.
Append the output into a file named 'switch_output.txt'.
Store the file inside vars/systems.

tasks.title: Display First Lines of a File
steps: Display the first three lines of /etc/resolv.conf.
Overwrite the contents of a file named 'dns_output.txt'.
Store the file inside vars/systems.

tasks.title: Identify File Types
steps: Use the file command on '/etc/passwd'.
Use the file command on '/bin/ls'.
Store both outputs in a file named 'output_file' inside vars/systems/logs.

completion_message: Cool!!!! Great Job. You have successfully completed Linux Filesystem Management Lab.
